answers: A former well-known Canadian TV sports anchor is in jail after police say he robbed two banks in as many days in the western province of Alberta last week. Police in the small city of Medicine Hat say Steve Vogelsang robbed a Royal Bank of Canada on Thursday, Oct. 19, and then turned around the next day and robbed a Bank of Montreal, CBC reports. He entered both banks without a disguise and after demanding money, left with an undisclosed sum. Police finally arrested Vogelsang at a nearby hotel at around 3am on Saturday. Per CTV Winnipeg News, Vogelsang, 53, was a longtime news director and sports broadcaster at CKY, now CTV Winnipeg. He also taught journalism at Red River College in Winnipeg from 2002 to 2011. Conor Lloyd, a spokesman for the college, says, “I can confirm he is no longer an employee here.” Vogelsang is scheduled to appear in provincial court on Tuesday.

**Summary of News:**

Steve Vogelsang, a former Winnipeg broadcast personality and journalism instructor at Red River College, has been charged with two counts of robbery in connection with bank robberies in Medicine Hat, Alberta. The 53-year-old was arrested on October 26 at a hotel in Medicine Hat, just days after the alleged crimes, which occurred on October 19 and 20. According to police, Vogelsang entered a Royal Bank of Canada and a Bank of Montreal without a disguise, handed a note to a teller, and left with an undisclosed amount of cash. No weapons were seen during the incidents, but the police emphasized the threat posed by the note in a sensitive financial setting.

Vogelsang had a long career in broadcasting, serving as a news director and sports anchor at CKY-TV, now known as CTV Winnipeg, from the early 1990s until 2002. He later became a journalism instructor at Red River College from 2002 to 2011. After leaving the college, he and his wife moved to Nelson, British Columbia, where they owned three properties. However, they faced significant financial difficulties, including a $85,000 loss from selling those properties. Vogelsang and his wife also owned a home in Winnipeg, which was supposed to be transferred to him in September 2023 after removing his ex-wife’s name from the mortgage. However, she alleges he forged her signature and renewed the mortgage in both their names, leading to the home being foreclosed in April 2023.

Vogelsang has also been involved in legal and personal disputes. In March 2017, a former student he had dated off and on since 2004 obtained a protection order against him after he allegedly continued to contact her despite police requests to stop. Vogelsang is set to fight these allegations in court next month, claiming the woman has misled police and interfered in his life. He also faced a sexual assault charge in 2016, which was stayed in 2017, and three charges of disobeying a court order in 2017, which are expected to be addressed in court next year.

In addition to the robbery charges, Vogelsang has been dealing with financial and legal challenges, including mortgage issues and a divorce. He had previously planned to move to Vancouver Island in August 2023 and was working
